A.text: A man in a balloon rising vertically with an acceleration of 4.9 m/sec² releases a ball 2 sec after the balloon is let go from the ground. The greatest height above the ground reached by the ball is (g = 9.8 m/sec²)

Solution: Answer (1)
Height travelled by ball (with balloon) in 2 sec
h₁ = (1/2)at² = (1/2) × 4.9 × 2² = 9.8m
Velocity of the balloon after 2 sec
v = at = 4.9 × 2 = 9.8 m/s
Now if the ball is released from the balloon then it acquire same velocity in upward direction.
Let it move up to maximum height h₂
v² = u² − 2gh₂ ⇒ 0 − (9.8)² − 2 × (9.8) × h₂ = h₂ = 4.9 m
Greatest height above the ground reached by the ball = h₁ + h₂ = 9.8 + 4.9 = 14.7 m

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: For a beam of electrons, accelerated from rest by a potential difference V₁, the de-Broglie wavelength of the electron is λ. If the electrons are further retarded through potential difference V₂, then de-Broglie wavelength of the electron becomes 3λ. Find the ratio V₂/V₁
A.sol_text:
Let K₁ be kinetic energy of electron, when it is accelerated from rest by a potential difference V₁.
∴ K₁ = eV₁
So momentum of electron, P₁ = √(2K₁m)
= √(2eV₁m)
Here m is mass of electron
∴ λ = h/p₁
⇒ λ = h/√(2eV₁m) ...(i)

Now let K₂ be kinetic energy of electron when it is retarded through a potential difference V₂
∴ K₂ = eV₁ - eV₂
K₂ = e(V₁ - V₂)

So, momentum of electron, P₂ = √(2K₂m)
= √(2e(V₁ - V₂)m)
∴ de-Broglie wavelength of electron,
3λ = h/p₂
⇒ 3λ = h/√(2e(V₁ - V₂)m) ...(ii)

From (i) and (ii)
3h/√(2eV₁m) = h/√(2e(V₁ - V₂)m)

⇒ 9(V₁ - V₂) = V₁
8V₁ = 9V₂
⇒ V₂/V₁ = 8/9

Nitrogen forms a wide range of oxides, exhibiting +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5 oxidation state.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: From the following given compounds select the one which will have maximum percentage of enol form in keto-enol tautomerism.
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)

Solution:

The enol form of compound (1) can form intramolecular H-bonding (shown with a hydrogen bond between the enol OH and the adjacent C=O group), which provides stability to the molecule. This stabilization shifts the keto-enol equilibrium toward the enol form.

Compound (2) has a phenyl group (Ph) attached to the central carbon. Because of this bulky group, the stability of the enol form decreases due to steric hindrance.

Compound (3) (acetaldehyde, CH₃—CHO) does not show intramolecular H-bonding and has no special stabilization of the enol form.

Compound (4) has a methyl group (CH₃) attached to the central carbon. This group decreases the stability of the enol form.

Compound (1) has the maximum stability of its enol form due to intramolecular H-bonding, resulting in the maximum percentage of enol form in keto-enol tautomerism.

A.text:
Consider the compounds:

(a) and (b) marked on structure

A.sol_text:

x → γ − x

⇒ cos(γ − x) = −cos x ⇒ γ = (2n + 1)π ...(vi)
and sin x + sin(x − γ) = 0
⇒ sin x = −sin(x − γ)
⇒ sin(γ − x) = sin x ⇒ γ = (2n + 1)π ...(vii)
(vi) and (vii)
⇒ cos γ = −1
∴ (β cos γ)/α = −1

A.text: For x ∈ R, x ≠ 0, if y(x) is a differentiable function such that x∫_1^x y(t)dt = (x+1)∫_1^x ty(t)dt, then y(x) equals (where C is a constant)
A.sol_text:
x∫_1^x y(t)dt = x∫_1^x ty(t)dt + ∫_x^t ty(t)dt
Differentiate w.r.t x

∫_1^x y(t)dt = ∫_1^x ty(t)dt + x^2y(x)
Differentiate again w.r.t x

(1-3x)y(x) = x^2y'(x)

(1/y)(dy/dx) = (1-3x)/x^2

Integrating on both sides
⇒ log y = -1/x - 3 log x + c
⇒ log(yx^3) = -1/x + c
⇒ yx^3 = e^(-1/x + c)
⇒ y = (e^(-1/x + c))/x^3
⇒ y = (C/x^3)e^(-1/x)

A.text: Let a, b and λ be positive real numbers. Suppose P is an end point of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = 4λ x, and suppose the ellipse (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1 passes through the point P. If the tangents to the parabola and the ellipse at the point P are perpendicular to each other, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
A.sol_text:
Equation of tangent to parabola y² = 4λx at P (λ, 2λ) is : y·2λ = 2λ(x + λ)
∴ x − y + λ = 0
∴ Slope of tangent = 1

and equation of tangent at P to ellipse (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1 is :
(xλ/a²) + (y·2λ/b²) = 1

∴ Slope of tangent = (−b²)/(2λa²)
∴ 1 · (−b²)/(2λa²) = −1
⇒ b²/a² = 2

∴ Eccentricity of ellipse = √(1 − a²/b²)
= √(1 − 1/2) = 1/√2

∴ Ellipse (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1 passes through (λ, 2λ)
Hence b² > a²

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A letter is known to have come either from "KRISHNAGIRI" or "DHARMAPURI", on the post mark only the two consecutive letters "RI" are visible. Then the chance that it came from "KRISHNAGIRI" is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Solution:
Let E₁ and E₂ be events that the letter came from "DHARMAPURI", "KRISHNAGIRI" respectively
⇒ P(E₁) = P(E₂) = 1/2
Let "A" be the event that two consecutive letters "RI" are visible on post mark
P(A/E₁) = 1/9 (∵ there is only one "RI" present)
P(A/E₂) = 2/10 = 1/5 (∵ there are two "RI" present)
By Bayes theorem
P(E₂/A) = P(E₂)P(A/E₂) / [P(E₁)P(A/E₁) + P(E₂)P(A/E₂)]
= [(1/2 × 1/5)] / [(1/2 × 1/9) + (1/2 × 1/5)]
= 9/14

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: If a, b, c are real numbers such that 0 < a < 1, 0 < b < 1, 0 < c < 1, a + b + c = 2, then the least value of (a)/(1-a) + (b)/(1-b) + (c)/(1-c) is equal to
B.sol_text:
Answer: 8

Solution:
Suppose a = y + z, b = z + x, c = x + y
∴ a + b + c = 2 (given)
⇒ 2(x + y + z) = 2
⇒ x + y + z = 1

∴ a = y + z = 1 − x ⇒ x = 1 − a
b = z + x = 1 − y ⇒ y = 1 − b
c = x + y ⇒ c = 1 − z ⇒ z = 1 − c

Also, 0 < a < 1, 0 < b < 1, 0 < c < 1
⇒ 1 − a > 0, 1 − b > 0, 1 − c > 0
⇒ x > 0, y > 0, z > 0

Now, (a)/(1-a) + (b)/(1-b) + (c)/(1-c) = ((y+z)(z+x)(x+y))/(xyz) ... (i)

Also, A.M. ≥ G.M.
⇒ (y+z)/2 ≥ √(yz) ⇒ (y+z)/√(yz) ≥ 2... (ii)

⇒ (z+x)/2 ≥ √(zx) ⇒ (z+x)/√(zx) ≥ 2... (iii)

and (x+y)/2 ≥ √(xy) ⇒ (x+y)/√(xy) ≥ 2... (iv)

Multiplying (ii), (iii) and (iv) we get,
((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))/(xyz) ≥ 8... (v)

∴ From (i) and (v) we get,
(a)/(1-a) + (b)/(1-b) + (c)/(1-c) ≥ 8
